english.title: Obstruct / assault a clergyman / minister in discharge of duties in place of worship / burial place
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF THE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 36 of the Offences against the Person Act 1861.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
by threat / force
obstruct / prevent endeavoured to obstruct / prevent,
clergyman / minister
in / from celebrating divine service or officiating
in a church / chapel / meeting house / place of divine worship OR
in / from the performance of his / her duty
in lawful burial of the dead in a churchyard / burial place OR
struck / offered violence to / upon civil process OR
under the pretence of executing civil process
arrested a clergyman / minister
engaged in / to his / her knowledge about to engage in
rites / duties OR
to his / her going to perform rites / duties OR
returning from performance of rites / duties

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the prescribed sum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment.

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
